title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is the canonical reference for employees, managers, and approvers. The People Ops team owns policy maintenance; Security and Finance are listed as primary partners for sections below.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who access Redwood systems, data, or funding. Exceptions require documented approval from the owner_team and the relevant risk owner (Security, Finance, or Legal).

Table of contents
1) Access & Permissions
2) Change Management
3) Data Management & Classification
4) Procurement & Expenses
5) Vendor Management
6) Travel Policy
7) Internal Templates and Request Forms
8) Ownership, Review Cadence, and Escalations

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and auditable approvals.
Key principles:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) by default.
- Principle of least privilege: users receive the minimum permissions needed to perform their job for the duration required.
- Just-in-time (JIT) privileged elevation for sensitive operations.
- All access requests and changes must be recorded in the access request tracker (see templates section).

Access types and owners:
- Corporate resources (Google Workspace, Okta, Slack, Confluence): Owner: people-ops.
- Production infra and runtime (Kubernetes, GPU pools, internal APIs): Owner: eng-platform with Security as co-owner for approvals.
- Secrets and keys (KMS/HSM access): Owner: security-and-compliance.

Onboarding checklist (people-ops):
1. Submit access request via Access Request template (link in Templates).
2. Manager approves required roles and duration.
3. Security reviews sensitive access requests (prod, secrets).
4. Account provisioning is performed by People Ops/IT with Okta and SCIM provisioning.
5. Confirm MFA, corporate device enrollment, and disk encryption.

Offboarding checklist (people-ops):
1. Revoke Okta account and deprovision SCIM immediately on termination date.
2. Rotate credentials for any service-accounts owned by departing employee within 24 hours.
3. Confirm return of corporate devices or initiate remote wipe.
4. Update on-call rosters and ownership documents.

Privileged access escalation and emergency access:
- Emergency (break-glass) access requires a documented approval by at least one engineering manager and one security lead after-the-fact review within 24 hours.
- JIT elevation sessions are time-limited (max 2 hours) and recorded in session logs.

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly automated recertification for all high-risk groups (production access, secrets).
- Semi-annual review for group memberships and app-level roles.

Example access request YAML (use in Access Request template):

requester: "first.last@redwood.com"
requested_roles:
  - "k8s-prod-read"
  - "redwood-console-deployer"
justification: "Working on rollout for model-v2; needs deploy access for canary testing"
duration_days: "7"
approvals:
  manager: "manager@redwood.com"
  security: "security-lead@redwood.com"

2) Change Management
Purpose: Reduce operational risk and ensure traceability for all infrastructure and service changes.
Change categories:
- Standard change: Pre-approved, low-risk, repeatable (e.g., certificate renewals, scheduled backups). Implemented by owner with automated logging. Review timeframe: documented; no CAB required.
- Normal change: Any change that modifies production services or infra (deploys, schema migrations). Requires RFC, risk assessment, and CAB review if high impact. Target review time: 48 business hours.
- Emergency change: Critical fixes to restore service. Implement immediately with post-change RCA and retrospective. Post-approval within 24 hours.

Change process (normal change):
1. Requestor files RFC using the Change Request template (link in Templates) including rollback plan, owners, and runbook.
2. Engineering reviewer performs a risk assessment and assigns category.
3. If CAB required, schedule next CAB meeting (weekly cadence). CAB membership: Engineering leads, Eng SRE, Security, Product representative, Change Manager.
4. Approval recorded in the RFC and ticket system; schedule change window and notify stakeholders via status page and Slack #ops-alerts.
5. Execute change; capture metrics (latency, error rate) and perform smoke tests.
6. If failure occurs, follow rollback plan and open an incident if SLOs are violated.
7. Post-change review within 3 business days to capture lessons and update runbooks.

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Standard change windows: 02:00-05:00 UTC weekdays for infra work.
- Blackout periods: Major launch windows and scheduled customer-facing events. Blackouts published on the company calendar; changes require Exec approval during blackout.

Rollback and testing:
- All normal changes must include an explicit rollback plan and one staging rehearsal before production.
- For schema migrations, use backward-compatible rollout where possible and feature flags.

3) Data Management & Classification
Purpose: Protect customer and company data, ensure regulatory compliance, and minimize risk of data loss.
Data classification levels:
- Public: Data intended for public consumption.
- Internal: Internal operational data (default).
- Confidential: Business-sensitive information (financial forecasts, non-public product roadmaps).
- Restricted: Customer personal data, regulated data, or data subject to legal/contractual controls.

Handling requirements by classification:
- Encryption: At-rest and in-transit encryption required for Confidential and Restricted.
- Access: Role-based access with Security review for Restricted.
- Retention: Follow retention schedule below; retention exceptions require Legal approval.

Retention schedule (examples):
| Data type | Classification | Retention | Owner |
|----------|----------------|-----------|-------|
| Audit logs | Restricted | 7 years | eng-sre |
| CI build artifacts | Internal | 90 days | eng-infra |
| Payroll records | Confidential | 7 years | finance-legal |
| Customer chat transcripts | Restricted | 2 years (unless contract states otherwise) | customer-success |

Backups and restore SLAs:
- Critical production databases: RPO <= 1 hour; RTO <= 4 hours. Backup ownership: eng-platform.
- Object storage backups: daily snapshots retained 30 days; longer retention per contract.
- Restore exercises: Quarterly restore drills for critical data stores; results reported to SRE and Security.

Data transfer and third-party processors:
- Any transfer of Restricted data to third parties requires a Data Processing Agreement and Security assessment (see Vendor Management).
- Cross-region replication must be approved by Security and Data Privacy.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Provide predictable controls for company spend while enabling teams to move quickly.
Spending thresholds and approval matrix:
- <$1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000- $10,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- $10,000- $100,000: Finance + Legal + Director approval.
- >$100,000: VP-level approval and Contract review.

Corporate card policy:
- Cardholders must be approved by manager and Finance; issuance requires completion of expense policy training.
- Monthly reconciliation due within 7 business days of statement; missing receipts will trigger review and possible card suspension.

Purchasing process (steps):
1. Submit Purchase Request template with business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement reviews quotes and -- for >$10k -- requests at least 2 competitive bids where feasible.
3. Finance approves budget and issues PO.
4. Vendor receives PO and delivers product/service; Finance confirms invoice and processes payment within standard terms.

Expense reimbursement:
- Use the Expenses template to submit receipts within 30 days.
- Per diem and business travel rules apply (see Travel section).

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Ensure vendors meet security, performance, and contractual requirements.
Vendor onboarding steps:
1. Submit Vendor Onboarding template with scope and data needs.
2. Procurement and Security perform vendor assessment: security questionnaire, data classification review, and reference checks for critical services.
3. Legal reviews contract terms and negotiates Data Processing Agreement (DPA) when handling Restricted data.
4. Finance approves payment terms and PO issuance.
5. Add vendor to vendor registry and track contract renewal dates.

Security assessment checklist (minimum):
- SOC2/ISO certifications where applicable.
- Data encryption at rest and in transit.
- Vulnerability management and patch cadence.
- Incident response SLAs and notification timelines (max 24 hours for security incidents).

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Tier 1 (critical): Vendors that process Restricted data or run production services. Require quarterly security reviews and exec-level sponsorship.
- Tier 2 (important): Vendors that support internal tools or process Internal/Confidential data. Annual reviews.
- Tier 3 (non-critical): Low-risk vendors (marketing tools, general subscriptions). Biennial reviews.

6) Travel Policy
Purpose: Provide clear, fair, and safe guidance for business travel, while controlling costs.
Booking and approvals:
- Domestic travel: Manager approval for trips >$500. International travel: Manager + People Ops pre-approval.
- Use preferred vendors (corporate travel portal) for flights and hotels where available to ensure corporate rates and insurance coverage.

Per diem and allowable expenses:
- Domestic per diem: $75/day for meals.
- International per diem: $150/day for meals.
- Lodging: Book standard room class; upgrades require prior approval and justification.
- Ground transportation: Use rideshares or taxis; car rentals require safety justification and approval for one-way rentals.

Safety and security:
- Register international travel with People Ops for emergency support.
- Emergency contact: People Ops travel lead (travel@redwood.com).
- Insurance: Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation and emergency assistance for approved trips.

Expense submission and receipts:
- Submit the Travel Expense template within 10 business days of trip completion with all receipts.
- Missing receipts over $25 require an explanation; Finance may decline reimbursement otherwise.

7) Internal Templates and Request Forms
All templates are stored in Confluence Templates under the Policies space. Common templates: 
- Access Request (YAML example included above)
- Change Request / RFC
- Purchase Request
- Vendor Onboarding
- Travel Expense Submission
- Expense Reimbursement form
- Incident Postmortem template

Example: Change Request template fields (short):
- Title, Owner, Service Impact, Rollback Plan, Test Plan, Deployment Window, Monitoring Playbook, Approvals

8) Ownership, Review Cadence, and Escalations
- Policy owner: people-ops.
- Security reviews sections: access, data, vendor on-boarding.
- Finance reviews: procurement, cards, expense policies.
- Review cadence: Full policy review annually; targeted sections reviewed as follows: Access & Permissions: quarterly; Change Management: semi-annually; Data Management: annually or when regs change.

Escalation paths:
- Operational incidents: Pager/On-call procedures and SRE runbooks.
- Policy disputes: People Ops -> Director of People Ops -> COO.
- High-risk procurement or vendor disputes: Finance -> Legal -> CFO.

Appendices and quick links
- Quick link: Access Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request
- Quick link: Change Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-request
- Quick link: Vendor Onboarding: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/vendor-onboarding

Revision history
- 2024-11-15: Initial consolidated policy by People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- 2025-06-10: Added RPO/RTO targets and vendor tiers (reviewers Marco Li, Elena Gomez).
- 2026-02-10: Updated procurement thresholds and travel per diem amounts (last_updated).

Notes and exceptions
- Any deviation from these policies requires a documented exception request and approval from the policy owner and the relevant risk owner. Exceptions are recorded in the exceptions register.

Contact and feedback
For questions or suggested updates, file a Policy Change Request using the internal template or email policy-changes@redwood.com.
